name: The Content Engine: 12 Solo Founder Prompts
tagline: Turn a single raw idea into a full week of strategic, conversion-focused social media content.
metaDescription: Transform one idea into a week of high-converting social media posts with 12 plug-and-play AI prompts designed specifically for busy solo founders.
description:
# The Content Engine for Solo Founders

If you are a solo founder wearing every hat in your business, consistency on social media often feels impossible. You have great insights, but staring at a blank screen trying to turn one idea into a week of engaging posts wastes hours of valuable time.

This digital product solves the blank-page problem permanently. **The Content Engine** gives you 12 field-tested prompts specifically calibrated for B2B and SaaS solo founders. Instead of generic AI writing advice, these prompts use structured constraints to extract your actual expertise, industry insights, and product value.

### Who It's For
Solo founders, bootstrapped entrepreneurs, and indie makers who need to build an audience and drive signups without spending 15 hours a week on content creation.

### The Problem It Solves
Eliminates the exhausting cycle of reinventing the wheel for every post. You take one raw thought—like a customer question or a product feature update—feed it into these modular prompts, and instantly generate a week-long multi-platform content calendar.

### Why These Prompts Work
They rely on proven copywriting frameworks (like PAS, BAB, and story-driven arcs) combined with strict tone constraints to prevent the dreaded "AI voice." Each prompt includes a specific usage tip to ensure your authentic founder voice shines through every single post.

1 Notion template with embedded prompt workflows and content calendar
Compatible with ChatGPT, Claude, and all major LLMs
sampleItems: Context: My latest product update allows users to export data to CSV with a single click. Task: Write a LinkedIn thought-leadership post using the Before-After-Bridge framework...
Context: A customer told us our onboarding is the fastest they have ever used. Task: Write a punchy X (Twitter) thread breaking down our 3-step onboarding philosophy...

items.title: The Authority Thread
items.body: Act as an expert content marketer. Take the following raw founder insight and expand it into a 5-part X thread. Structure: Hook (bold statement challenging industry norms), Context (why this matters now), Core Lesson (actionable step 1 and 2), Proof (a brief hypothetical or real metric), CTA (invite replies or follows). Tone: Direct, no fluff, authoritative. Input insight: [INSERT IDEA HERE]. Usage tip: Edit the hook to match your personal writing cadence before publishing.

items.title: The Contrarian Take
items.body: Act as a pragmatic indie founder. Write a LinkedIn post challenging a common industry best practice related to this topic: [INSERT TOPIC]. Structure: Start with a 1-sentence provocative opening. Provide three bullet points explaining why the traditional advice fails solo operators. Conclude with a balanced alternative framework that actually works. Tone: Professional yet conversational, confident, and grounded in real-world bootstrapping experience. Usage tip: Best used on Tuesday mornings for maximum B2B engagement.

items.title: The Customer Problem Deep-Dive
items.body: Act as a direct-response copywriter. Write a 200-word newsletter section addressing a painful bottleneck our target audience faces: [INSERT PAIN POINT]. Use the Problem-Agitate-Solution (PAS) framework. Empathize with the solo founder's struggle, agitate the hidden costs of ignoring the problem, and introduce our product approach as the logical resolution without sounding overly salesy. Usage tip: Insert this into your weekly email broadcast as the core value section.

items.title: The Behind-The-Scenes Build
items.body: Act as a transparent startup builder. Write a short-form social post sharing a recent failure, experiment, or unexpected learning from building [INSERT PRODUCT/FEATURE]. Structure: Hook about what went wrong, the realization moment, the fix implemented, and one takeaway for fellow builders. Tone: Vulnerable, authentic, and humble. Usage tip: Pair this post with a raw screenshot of your analytics dashboard or a rough whiteboard sketch.

items.title: The Framework Breakdown
items.body: Act as a visual content strategist. Outline a 5-slide educational carousel for LinkedIn or Instagram based on this concept: [INSERT CONCEPT]. For each slide, provide: Slide Title (max 6 words), Slide Body (max 30 words), and Visual Direction (what graphic asset or layout to use). Ensure the logical flow takes the reader from a beginner misunderstanding to an advanced tactical execution. Usage tip: Plug these slide texts directly into a Canva template.

items.title: The FAQ Objection Crusher
items.body: Act as a high-converting SaaS copywriter. Write an objection-handling post targeting prospects who hesitate to buy because of: [INSERT OBJECTION, e.g., 'it takes too long to set up']. Structure: State the objection neutrally. Deconstruct why that fear is valid. Explain how our product completely eliminates that friction point. End with a low-risk call to action. Tone: Empathetic, reassuring, and logical. Usage tip: Great for driving direct message conversations on LinkedIn.

items.title: The Quick Win Tip
items.body: Act as a pragmatic productivity coach. Write a punchy, single-paragraph tip that gives our audience an immediate tactical win regarding: [INSERT SKILL/TOPIC]. The tip must be implementable in under 5 minutes. Tone: Energetic, clear, and encouraging. Usage tip: Perfect for a quick Thursday afternoon post when audience attention spans are shorter.

items.title: The Metric Milestone
items.body: Act as a bootstrapped founder celebrating a quiet milestone. Write a short post announcing this achievement: [INSERT METRIC, e.g., 'reaching 500 active users']. Instead of just flexing the number, share the single biggest mistake we made along the way to get here and thank a specific type of early adopter. Tone: Grateful, grounded, and inspiring. Usage tip: Tag 2 or 3 supportive peers or early beta users in the comments.

items.title: The Future Prediction
items.body: Act as an industry analyst looking ahead at our market. Write a forward-looking prediction post about how [INSERT TREND] will change the way solo founders operate over the next 12 months. Structure: Bold prediction, 2 supporting arguments based on current shifts, and a question for the comments to spark community debate. Tone: Visionary, analytical, and forward-thinking. Usage tip: Respond to every comment within the first hour of posting to boost algorithmic reach.

items.title: The Analogous Metaphor
items.body: Act as a creative storyteller. Explain a complex feature or technical concept of our product—[INSERT FEATURE]—using an unexpected, everyday metaphor (e.g., comparing database indexing to organizing a kitchen pantry). Keep the post under 150 words. Tone: Witty, accessible, and clever. Usage tip: This format consistently outperforms standard product update announcements because it stops the scroll.

items.title: The Resource Roundup
items.body: Act as a generous curator. Write a resource recommendation post listing 3 tools, books, or workflows that have dramatically improved my workflow as a solo founder in this category: [INSERT CATEGORY]. For each item, include the name and a 1-sentence explanation of why it's worth their time. Tone: Helpful, unselfish, and peer-to-peer. Usage tip: Do not include affiliate links in the main post; build trust first.

items.title: The Direct Pitch
items.body: Act as a conversion copywriter launching a focused sales post. Write a short, high-impact promotional post for our core offer: [INSERT PRODUCT/OFFER]. Structure: The primary pain point we solve, the exact mechanism of how we solve it in 3 steps, social proof or testimonial snippet, and a clear link-in-bio or comment-to-DM call to action. Tone: Direct, confident, and professional. Usage tip: Save this format for once a week, ideally on a Wednesday.
